acceptance_criteria.criterion: GET /api/repos returns all declared repositories from the registry file.
POST /api/repos creates a new repository entry with validated id (slug regex), unique id, and no folder_names conflicts; returns 400 with clear error on conflict.
PUT /api/repos/:repoId updates label, folder_names, and vision fields; enforces folder_name uniqueness across all entries.
DELETE /api/repos/:repoId removes the entry from the registry without deleting any project data.
GET /api/repos/:repoId returns the full repository entry or 404 if not found.
Folder names are unique across all repository entries — the API rejects create/update operations that would violate this constraint.

summary: Created mcp-server/gui/api-repos.ts: domain-split handler module following the api-knowledge.ts pattern, exporting handleListRepos, handleGetRepo, handleCreateRepo, handleUpdateRepo, handleDeleteRepo.
handleListRepos: loads registry via loadRegistry(), maps entries to RepoListItem shape (id, label, folder_names, has_vision, created_at, last_modified). Returns [] on empty/absent registry.
handleGetRepo: loads registry, finds entry by id, throws NOT_FOUND (404) for unknown repoId.

handleCreateRepo: validates body via RepoCreateBodySchema (Zod .strict()), enforces id uniqueness, enforces folder_name uniqueness via assertNoFolderNameConflicts(), defaults vision to all-null, persists via saveRegistry(). Returns 201 with the new entry.

handleUpdateRepo: loads registry, checks NOT_FOUND, validates body via RepoUpdateBodySchema (.strict()), enforces folder_name uniqueness excluding the entry being updated (self-conflict allowed), merges partial updates, sets last_modified. Persists via saveRegistry().
handleDeleteRepo: loads registry, checks NOT_FOUND, filters out the entry, persists. Returns { deleted: true }. Does NOT delete any project files.

Wired into mcp-server/gui/server.ts: import block added, three body-free routes in matchRoute() (GET /api/repos, GET /api/repos/:repoId, DELETE /api/repos/:repoId), two body-parsing routes in handleRequest() (POST /api/repos returns 201, PUT /api/repos/:repoId returns 200). Route summary comment updated.

Created mcp-server/tests/gui/api-repos.test.ts: 46 tests covering all 6 ACs — CRUD operations, validation, folder name conflict rejection, 404 for missing repos, has_vision computation, persistence verification, error shape.
TypeScript compilation: zero errors (tsc --noEmit).
Full test suite: 3046 tests pass, zero failures, zero regressions.

comments.note: api-repos.ts does not re-export the Zod schemas (RepoCreateBodySchema, RepoUpdateBodySchema) with explicit export — they are exported for test use but could be marked @internal in JSDoc if the intent is for handler use only. Low risk: the schemas are consumed only in tests for now.

handleUpdateRepo with an empty body ({}) is accepted as valid (all fields optional) and produces a no-op update that still sets last_modified. This is correct per the WP spec but may surprise callers expecting a 400 on a completely empty update. Could add a guard clause requiring at least one field to be present if the product team later decides it's confusing.

POST /api/repos returns 201 Created (not 200), consistent with REST conventions. The existing knowledge and project mutation handlers return 200 uniformly. This is the correct HTTP practice but is a mild inconsistency with the rest of the server's mutation responses. The server.ts body-parsing block for POST /api/repos explicitly passes 201, so this is intentional and traceable.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified through 46 unit tests — 46/46 pass. Full regression suite: 3046/3046 tests pass (zero regressions). TypeScript compiles clean (tsc --noEmit, exit 0).
AC-1 (GET /api/repos): handleListRepos returns [] on empty registry and full RepoListItem array when entries exist, including has_vision boolean, created_at, last_modified.

AC-2 (POST /api/repos): handleCreateRepo validates id via SLUG_REGEX, rejects duplicate id and empty label/folder_names, enforces folder_name uniqueness, defaults vision to all-null, returns created entry. Server wires it with HTTP 201.

AC-3 (PUT /api/repos/:repoId): handleUpdateRepo supports partial updates (label/folder_names/vision), preserves unchanged fields, always sets last_modified, persists correctly. Rejects empty label, empty folder_names array, and unknown fields.

AC-4 (DELETE /api/repos/:repoId): handleDeleteRepo removes only the named entry from registry, leaving other entries untouched. Does NOT delete any project data. Released folder_names become reusable. Returns { deleted: true }.
AC-5 (GET /api/repos/:repoId): handleGetRepo returns full RepositoryEntry for known id, throws NOT_FOUND (→ 404) for unknown or when registry is empty.

AC-6 (folder_name uniqueness): assertNoFolderNameConflicts() blocks create and update operations that would introduce a folder_name already owned by another entry. Error message identifies the conflicting name(s). Self-conflict on update (re-setting existing names) is correctly allowed via excludeId.

Route wiring verified in server.ts: GET, DELETE wired in matchRoute(); POST (/api/repos, 201) and PUT (/api/repos/:repoId, 200) as explicit body-parsing early-return blocks in handleRequest(). apiErrorToStatus maps NOT_FOUND→404 and VALIDATION_ERROR→400 correctly.

comments.note: handleUpdateRepo with an empty body {} is a no-op update that still bumps last_modified. Correct per WP spec (all fields optional), but callers may find it surprising. Worth a product decision if a minimum-one-field guard is desired.

POST /api/repos returns 201 Created while all other mutation routes return 200. Intentional and correctly documented in server.ts comments. Mild inconsistency with the rest of the server, but correct REST practice.

No edge-case test for URL-encoded repoId in GET/DELETE route handlers (e.g., repo%2Did). decodeURIComponent is called at the server.ts routing level, so it works at runtime, but there is no unit-level test exercising the decode path. Low risk — hyphens in IDs are valid SLUG_REGEX matches and wouldn't normally be percent-encoded.

summary: Reviewed api-repos.ts, server.ts (repo-related sections), and api-repos.test.ts against all four review dimensions (Maintainability, Best Practices, Performance, Future Context). No blocking issues found.

Maintainability: Excellent. Domain-split pattern is consistent with api-knowledge.ts. Functions are single-purpose, well-named, and fully JSDoc'd. assertNoFolderNameConflicts is a clean, testable helper. toListItem is a pure shape-conversion function with no side effects.

Best Practices: Strong. Zod .strict() schemas guard both POST and PUT bodies. The double-parse approach (safeParse → RepositoryEntrySchema.parse) is belt-and-suspenders and matches the project convention. created_at is never mutated in handleUpdateRepo. The validationError helper reduces throw-site boilerplate.
Performance: No concerns. loadRegistry/saveRegistry on each request is the established project pattern for a small JSON registry file.

Future Context / Technical Debt: The repoPutMatch regex in handleRequest() is a hardcoded literal; the GET/DELETE repos routes use the segment-based matchRoute() instead. This is intentional (body-parsing routes must be in handleRequest), correctly commented, and matches the same pattern used by PATCH /api/knowledge/:id and POST /api/knowledge/:id/move — no concern.

Fix-Forward applied: Added @internal documentation to both exported Zod schemas (RepoCreateBodySchema, RepoUpdateBodySchema) clarifying their test-only export intent. Non-behavioral — no logic changed.

Documentation-Forward: The RepoListItem interface and has_vision computed field would benefit from an explicit entry in any API reference doc that gets generated for this server. Flagged for Documentation agent.

comments.note: Added '@internal' JSDoc note to the exported RepoCreateBodySchema and RepoUpdateBodySchema comments in api-repos.ts. These schemas are exported so tests can construct validated shapes directly, but are not part of the stable public API. The clarification prevents future consumers from treating the export as a committed interface. No logic was changed.

[documentation-forward] The RepoListItem interface (has_vision boolean computed from the three vision horizon fields) is not self-discoverable from the REST API surface without reading the source. If an API reference document exists or is planned for the GUI server endpoints, add an entry for GET /api/repos and GET /api/repos/:repoId that documents the RepoListItem vs RepositoryEntry shape distinction and explains that has_vision is a server-computed convenience field.

handleUpdateRepo accepts an empty body {} as a valid no-op that still bumps last_modified. Flagged by both Developer and QA as a known design decision. If the product team later decides a minimum-one-field guard is desirable, the fix is a single z.refine() added to RepoUpdateBodySchema. No action needed now.
